label: Puppet History
tagline: Round-headed cut-out puppets act out 'you are now a...' history on flat illustrated sets, cards and maps.

messages.mascot: Mascots are not available in the Puppet History style: its whole cast is house puppets, and one more character would be confused with them. Choose another visual style, or no mascot.

review:
- This video is in the Puppet History style, and the following are its intended, approved look: cut-out puppets with big round white heads, dot eyes, short brows, blush and a small mouth, pill arms and white mitten hands, framed from the waist up behind a foreground band; generic era costumes and hats; flat warm illustrated sets (a farm, a street, an office, a palace hall, a castle wall, a ship's deck, a market, a factory, an army camp, a laboratory, a classroom, a field) with dark brown ink outlines and no gradients; hard cuts between beats; puppets sliding in from the frame's edge and stopping dead; a costume changing on a hard cut as a gag; a cream sign held in front of a puppet's chest; a name plate under a puppet; a typed document card with a red stamp landing and a line struck out with a new value scrawled in red; a flat map of today's countries with regions filling in, a curved arrow growing and a hand-lettered label; a hand-lettered date in the corner. Every person is the same house puppet: a real, historical person is that puppet in a generic costume of their era with their name on the plate, and that is correct. Do NOT report any of these as defects, and do not suggest realistic people, likenesses, photographs, historical borders, smooth animation or gradients: their absence is the style.
- Do report: a puppet, costume, prop, card or map region that does not match what the narration says at that moment, a name plate on the wrong puppet, a costume or prop that copies a real uniform, insignia, flag or a real person's signature feature, a living person or a living leader named on a plate, a tragedy (a war atrocity, a disaster, deaths) played for laughs, text cut off or overflowing its sign, card, plate or label, puppets overlapping each other, anything cut off at the frame edge, text too small to read on a phone, a face that contradicts the line, and a stretch of more than about three seconds where nothing on screen changes.
script:
Every beat's `visual` is a **beat** brief: the set, card or map, which puppets are in it in which costumes, and what changes on the line ("camp: you, a legionary, salute"; "card: ENLISTMENT, PAY struck out to MINUS GEAR"; "map: Italy red, arrow to France, label GAUL").

The narration speaks to the viewer as "you", placed in a past era with a job, a rank or a rule ("You're a Roman legionary."). Tell it as a run of short beats with one change each: where you are, the paper you sign, the number that turns out worse than promised, the march across a map, the twist at the end. Write in short, wry sentences, and build to a reversal the picture can show (a costume swapped, a number struck out, a stamp landing). Every date, number, place and rule must be true and checkable. A real, historical person may appear only by name, as the house puppet in a costume of their era with a name plate: never a living person, never a leader of a regime still in power, and never a feature that would make the puppet look like them. Never play a tragedy for laughs: a war's dead, a disaster, a persecution, a famine are told plainly or left out, never as a gag. Maps show today's countries: name a historical region by the modern countries it covers.

picture.opening: Frame 0 shows the first set with the first puppet already in place in its era costume, or a document card or a map already drawn. Never an empty set.
picture.turn: A hard cut to a new beat on the first word of a turn or a re-opening, or a puppet entering, acting, swapping costume or holding up a sign, or a stamp landing, on that word.
picture.payoff: The reversal: a costume swapped on a hard cut, a number struck out with the new one scrawled, or a stamp landing, with the strongest face.
picture.ending: Hold the last beat to the last frame. No sign-off card after it.

best_for: 'you are now a...' history told to the viewer in the second person: a job, a rank or a rule in a past era
daily life and work in a past era (a Roman legionary, a medieval peasant, a 1920s factory worker)
why a historical event happened, told with light humour and a reversal at the end
who moved where on a map: an army's march, a trade route, a migration, shown on today's countries
avoid_for: the history of an invention, a discovery or one real person's life told calmly through time (Storybook Atlas fits it)
a fraud, a scam or a money dilemma with the viewer inside it (Case File Story fits it)
a real event told through pictures of the real ship, building or people (Photo Explainer fits it)
an invented hero with recurring scenes and no history (Illustrated fits it)
a living person, a living leader or a regime still in power
a topic whose subject is a war atrocity, a genocide, a disaster, a famine or another tragedy: this style plays history for a smile, and a tragedy is never played for laughs
routing.cannot_show: photographs, real likenesses or historical borders: every person is the house puppet in a generic era costume, with a name plate for a real one, and maps show today's countries
signals: the script speaks to the viewer as 'you' in a past era
a historical job, rank, contract or rule is the subject
the story turns on a reversal of costume, number or contract
people or armies move between places on a map
